lines: Generator for the dual tone multi-frequency pairs a telephone keypad sends, one of sixteen keys picked by pitch voltage and sounded while a gate is high
Sounds the tone while the voltage here is 1.7V or above, and silences the output below that; each fresh rising edge restarts the tone from its beginning
Picks which of the sixteen keys is sounded, a semitone per key and within 0.02V of each step: 0V gives 1, and then 2, 3, A, 4, 5, 6, B, 7, 8, 9, C, star, 0, hash and D at 1.25V
The two summed sine tones of the chosen key, and 0V whenever the gate is below 1.7V
DTMF.notes: The maker's manual prints the tone 5 twice in its key table, against F-4 and F#-4; the source gives 5 at F-4 and 6 at F#-4, which is the mapping described here.

lines: Noise generator producing white or pink noise for as long as a gate is high
Lets the noise through while the voltage here is 1.7V or above, and holds the output at 0V below that
Chooses white noise in the upper position and pink noise in the lower
The noise, white or pink as the switch is set, and 0V while the gate is below 1.7V
Four-step sequencer clocked from step to step, working over the 0-10V range that CV uses rather than the bipolar range a note sequencer covers
Advances to the next of the four steps on each rising edge through 1.7V
The voltage of the step the sequencer has reached, held until the next clock edge
Sets the voltage of that step in whole volts, 0 to 10V
Added to the knob of that step, the sum clamped to 0-10V
Inverter, either flipping the sign of a voltage or turning a gate into its opposite
The voltage to be inverted
In the CV position an input of 1.7V or more gives 0V out and anything lower gives 1.7V out; in the V/OCT position the sign of the input is flipped, so 3.4V in gives -3.4V out
The inverted voltage
Not.notes: No family on the two jacks: what they carry changes with the switch, a gate in the CV position and a bipolar voltage in the V/OCT position. The maker's manual describes the CV position backwards, saying 1.7V in gives 1.7V out; the source gives 0V for an input at or above 1.7V and 1.7V for anything below, which is what an inverter does and what is written here.

lines: Splits one input between two outputs under knob and CV control
The signal divided between the two outputs
Sets the division, -5 to +5: at either end one output carries the whole signal and the other nothing, and at 0 each carries half
Added to the PAN knob, the sum clamped to -5V and 5V
Carries the input scaled by the pan setting, nothing at -5 rising to the whole signal at +5
Carries the input scaled by the pan setting, the whole signal at -5 falling to nothing at +5
Adds a fixed voltage to a signal, offsetting it up or down; a waveform running -5V to 5V becomes a 0-10V CV source when shifted by 5V
The signal to be offset
In the CLIP position the result is clamped to -5V and 5V, and in the NATURAL position it is passed at whatever voltage it reaches
Sets the voltage added to the input, -5V to +5V
Added to the SHIFT knob, and the total is what the input is offset by
The input plus the shift amount, clamped to -5V and 5V when the switch is set to CLIP
Shift.notes: No family on IN or OUT: the module offsets audio and CV alike, so what the jacks carry is whatever is patched.

lines: Two oscillators blended into a single output, each with its own wave, start shift, octave, fine tuning, polarity and random dropping of cycles
Picks the wave that oscillator draws in whole steps, 0 sine, 1 triangle, 2 sawtooth and 3 square, with the name of the chosen wave shown in the green display for it
Added to the SHAPE knob of that oscillator, one volt per wave, so 1.3V with the knob on sine selects triangle
Shifts the starting point of that oscillator's wave, 0 for no shift and 10 for the largest; moving it restarts both oscillators from the start of their cycle
Added to the SHIFT knob of that oscillator, the sum clamped to the knob's 0 to 10 range
Transposes that oscillator in whole octaves, -4 to +4
Added to the OCTAVE setting of that oscillator at one volt per octave
Adds up to one volt either way to the pitch of that oscillator, which is a whole octave at each end of its travel
Half of the voltage here is added to the FINE setting of that oscillator
Sets how often that oscillator drops a cycle and gives 0V in its place, never at 0 and roughly one cycle in eight at 5
Half of the voltage here is added to the RANDOM setting of that oscillator, the sum clamped to 0 to 5
Flips the polarity of the wave from the left oscillator in its lower position, and leaves it upright in the upper
Flips the polarity of the wave from the right oscillator in its lower position, and leaves it upright in the upper
Sets the balance between the two oscillators, 0 for the left one alone, 10 for the right one alone and 5 for an even blend
Added to the MIX knob, the sum clamped to 0-10V
Sets the pitch both oscillators are built from before their own octave and fine settings; 0V gives C4 at 261.63Hz
The two oscillators blended as MIX sets, reaching 5V at its peak
Oscar2.notes: The right oscillator's shift is computed from the left oscillator's shift value in the source (Oscar2.cpp uses s1 where s2 is meant), so moving the right SHIFT knob restarts both oscillators without changing the right one's starting point. The line for SHIFT describes what the knob is for rather than this fault.

lines: Single-band equalizer with seven filter shapes, a frequency from 30Hz to 14000Hz and an adjustable bandwidth
The signal to be filtered
The filtered signal
Sets the frequency the filter works around, 30Hz to 14000Hz, with the frequency in use shown in the green display
Shifts the filter frequency, 10V adding the whole 30Hz to 14000Hz span to the FREQ knob and -10V taking it away
Picks the filter shape in whole steps, low pass, high pass, band pass, notch, peak, low shelf and high shelf, with the name shown in the green display
Sets the width of the band worked on, 0.1 to 6, a low value giving a wide band and a high value a narrow one
Shifts the Q, 10V adding the whole 0.1 to 6 span to the Q knob and -10V taking it away
Eq.notes: The maker's manual lists six filter shapes and omits peak; the source and the panel display carry seven, peak between notch and low shelf.

lines: Four-pole resonant low pass filter modelled on the Moog ladder, with frequency and resonance under knob and CV control
The signal to be filtered; with nothing patched here the output stays at 0V
Sets the cutoff frequency, 20Hz to 6000Hz, with the frequency in use shown in the green display
Each volt here moves the cutoff by 1000Hz, added to the FREQ knob and clamped to 20Hz and 6000Hz
Sets the resonance, 0 to 4, with the filter ringing hard towards the top of its travel
Each volt here adds 0.1 to the resonance, and the total is clamped to 0.1 and 4
The low pass output of the filter
Carbon.notes: The maker's manual gives the frequency range as 20Hz to 7000Hz; the installed 2.0.0 source configures the knob for 20Hz to 6000Hz and clamps the total there, which is what is written here.

lines: Eight channel stereo mixer, each channel with a level slider, a pan knob and solo and mute buttons, summed to a stereo pair with its own levels and mutes
The signal for that channel; an unpatched channel adds nothing to the mix
Sets the level of that channel, 0 to 1.2 with 1 passing it unchanged
Places that channel in the stereo field, the right side silent fully counter-clockwise, the left silent fully clockwise and both at full level at the centre
One press solos that channel and the next press releases it; while any channel is soloed, every channel that is not soloed is dropped from the mix
One press mutes that channel and the next press restores it, and the lamp is lit while it is muted
Sets the level of the left side of the stereo mix after the channels are summed, 0 to 1.2 with 1 passing it unchanged
Sets the level of the right side of the stereo mix after the channels are summed, 0 to 1.2 with 1 passing it unchanged
One press mutes the left side of the stereo mix and the next restores it, and the lamp is lit while it is muted
One press mutes the right side of the stereo mix and the next restores it, and the lamp is lit while it is muted
The left side of the stereo mix, after its own level and mute
The right side of the stereo mix, after its own level and mute
Eight channel stereo mixer with a CV input for every channel control and a send and return loop on each channel and on the stereo mix
The signal for that channel; an unpatched channel adds nothing to the mix
Sets the level of that channel, 0 to 1.2 with 1 passing it unchanged
Each volt here adds 0.1 to the level of that channel, and the total is clamped to 0 and 1.2
Places that channel in the stereo field, the right side silent fully counter-clockwise, the left silent fully clockwise and both at full level at the centre
Each volt here moves that channel a tenth of the way across the stereo field, added to its PAN knob
One press solos that channel and the next press releases it; while any channel is soloed, every channel that is not soloed is dropped from the mix
Each rising edge through 1.7V toggles the solo of that channel, the same latch the SOLO button works
One press mutes that channel and the next press restores it, and the lamp is lit while it is muted
Each rising edge through 1.7V toggles the mute of that channel, the same latch the MUTE button works
Carries that channel's input at the voltage it arrives, for feeding an effect module; it stops being updated while the channel is muted or dropped by another channel's solo
The return from the effect that channel was sent to, blended back into the channel by its MIX knob
Sets how much of that channel is taken from its return instead of its input, 0 for the dry input alone and 1 for the return alone
Each volt here adds 0.1 to the wet and dry balance of that channel, added to its MIX knob and clamped to 0 and 1
Sets the level of the left side of the stereo mix after the channels are summed, 0 to 1.2 with 1 passing it unchanged
Sets the level of the right side of the stereo mix after the channels are summed, 0 to 1.2 with 1 passing it unchanged
One press mutes the left side of the stereo mix and the next restores it, and the lamp is lit while it is muted
One press mutes the right side of the stereo mix and the next restores it, and the lamp is lit while it is muted
The left side of the stereo mix, after its return, its level and its mute
The right side of the stereo mix, after its return, its level and its mute
Carries the summed left side of the mix before its return is blended in, and stops being updated while the left side is muted
Carries the mix before the right return is blended in, and stops being updated while the right side is muted; the source sends the left side of the mix to this jack rather than the right
The return from the effect the left side of the mix was sent to, blended back by the LEFT MIX knob
The return from the effect the right side of the mix was sent to, blended back by the RIGHT MIX knob
Sets how much of the left side of the mix is taken from its return instead of the summed channels, 0 for the summed channels alone and 1 for the return alone
Sets how much of the right side of the mix is taken from its return instead of the summed channels, 0 for the summed channels alone and 1 for the return alone
Each volt here covers the whole wet and dry range of the left side of the mix, added to the LEFT MIX knob and clamped to 0 and 1
Each volt here covers the whole wet and dry range of the right side of the mix, added to the RIGHT MIX knob and clamped to 0 and 1
Each rising edge through 1.7V toggles the mute of the left side of the stereo mix
Each rising edge through 1.7V toggles the mute of the right side of the stereo mix
MixerCV.notes: The RIGHT SEND jack carries the left side of the mix: MixerCV.cpp sets MAIN_R_SEND from master_l, which looks like a copy of the line above it. The channel MIX CV is divided by ten before it is added to the knob, so 0-10V covers the range, while the LEFT MIX and RIGHT MIX CV inputs are added without that division, so 0-1V covers theirs.

lines: Two independent constant voltage sources, each switched on and off by hand
One press turns that half on and the next turns it off; the lamp is lit while it is on, and the output is held at 0V while it is off
Sets the voltage that half puts out while it is on, 0V to 10V
The voltage set for that half while it is switched on, and 0V while it is off
Two independent two-input mixers in one narrow panel, each crossfading between its pair of inputs
One of the two signals mixed in that half, carried alone when its MIX knob is fully counter-clockwise
One of the two signals mixed in that half, carried alone when its MIX knob is fully clockwise
Crossfades between the two inputs of that half, one alone at each end of its travel and both at half level at the centre
The two inputs of that half blended as its MIX knob sets
M.notes: The knob is printed MIX on the panel and the maker's tooltip calls it Volume; it crossfades between the two inputs rather than setting a level, which is what the panel name and the source both give.

lines: Routes one signal to either of two outputs, choosing between them by comparing a second voltage against a split point
The signal routed to one output or the other; with nothing patched here the modulator voltage is routed instead
The voltage compared against the split point to choose which output is used; with nothing patched here both outputs stay at 0V
In the UNI position the split point is read as 0V to 10V, and in the BI position 5V is taken off it so it runs -5V to 5V
Sets the voltage the modulator is compared against, 0 to 10 before the polarity switch shifts it
Shifts the split point, 10V adding the whole 0 to 10 span to the SPLIT knob and -10V taking it away
Adds a fixed offset of -10V to 10V to whatever leaves the LOW output
Shifts the LOW offset, 10V adding the whole -10V to 10V span to the LOW ATT knob and -10V taking it away
Adds a fixed offset of -10V to 10V to whatever leaves the HIGH output
Shifts the HIGH offset, 10V adding the whole -10V to 10V span to the HIGH ATT knob and -10V taking it away
Carries the signal while the modulator voltage is below the split point, with the LOW ATT offset added, and 0V at every other moment
Carries the signal while the modulator voltage is at or above the split point, with the HIGH ATT offset added, and 0V at every other moment
Tine.notes: LOW ATT and HIGH ATT are printed as attenuators and the maker's manual calls them that, but the source adds the knob value to the routed signal as an offset rather than scaling it; the lines describe what the source does. No family on AUD, LOW and HIGH: the module routes audio and CV alike, so what those jacks carry is whatever is patched.

lines: Compressor reducing anything that rises above a threshold, with ratio, attack and release
Sets the level above which the signal is reduced, 1V to 30V read from the envelope of the input
Sets how much of the excess above the threshold is kept, 1 passing the signal untouched and 10 keeping a tenth of the excess
Sets how quickly the envelope follower rises towards a louder input, 1ms to 100ms
Sets how quickly the envelope follower falls towards a quieter input, 1ms to 100ms
The signal to be compressed
The compressed signal
Two independent exciters, each blending its input with a saturated copy of it
The signal saturated in that half
Each volt here adds 0.1 to the wet and dry balance of that half, added to its MIX knob and clamped to 0 and 1
Sets the balance in that half, 0 passing the input untouched and 1 passing the saturated copy alone
The input of that half and its saturated copy blended as its MIX knob sets
Wave multiplier making eight delayed copies of one input and summing them into a running mix, with each copy also available on its own
The signal copied into all eight delay lines
Scales the input before it reaches the eight delay lines, 0 to 1
Shifts the delay of that copy, 10V adding the whole 0 to 1 span to its SHIFT knob and -10V taking it away
Sets the delay of that copy, 0 for none and 1 for a tenth of a second
Scales that delayed copy before it is added into the running mix, 0 to 1
The running mix of the delayed copies, summed down to and including that one
A polyphonic cable of eight channels, each carrying one delayed copy on its own after its LEVEL knob, with nothing summed
The full mix of all eight delayed copies
Tsunami.notes: Inputs 8 to 15 are declared in the module but are never placed on the panel and are never read by the source, so they carry no line, no tag and no family.
